findings.detail: Live feature RPC: XChainBridge enabled false, supported true (64 of 101 amendments enabled). All eight XChain transaction types carry featureXChainBridge as their gating amendment (transactions.macro 526-637); Transactor::invokePreflight returns temDISABLED when the gating amendment is not enabled (Transactor.h 409-425). No XChain transaction can execute on this network today.
findings.title: XChainBridge amendment disabled: every XChain transaction returns temDISABLED

findings.detail: XChainCreateBridge preflight requires the XRP issuing door to be the root account derived from the seed 'masterpassphrase' (r9cZA1mLK5R5Am25ArfXFmqgNwjZgnfk59). That account returns actNotFound (error 19) on the live ledger at ledger 8287774. A door account that does not exist cannot submit transactions, hold a SignerList, or receive funds, so an XRP-XRP bridge with PFTL as the issuing chain cannot be operated even if the amendment were enabled. The PFTL genesis account (r4vhrMChCsaoFsBoCkRTRGUuc1njfr7bmA) is a different address and would fail the same preflight check.
findings.title: The XRP issuing door the code requires does not exist on the live ledger

findings.detail: getSignersListAndQuorum reads sfSignerQuorum and the signer weights from the door account's signer-list object; the Bridge ledger entry carries no quorum field. The door owner can change the witness set and quorum via SignerListSet without touching the bridge object. The code states the consequence (XChainBridge.cpp 74-77): the witness servers are trusted 'in the sense that if a quorum of them collude, they can steal the funds put into trust.'
findings.title: Witness quorum lives in the door account's SignerList, not in the bridge object

findings.detail: ledger_entry for a fabricated bridge (genesis locking door, XRP issues, masterpassphrase root issuing door) returns entryNotFound (error 98). The genesis account owns zero ledger objects (account_objects count 0), so it owns no Bridge object. The XChain surface is entirely unexercised on this network.
findings.title: No bridge exists on the live ledger

findings.detail: onNewAttestations keeps one entry per signer account and replaces an old attestation when the same signer re-attests; claimHelper sums weights per signer, not per attestation, and requires weight >= quorum. Drill A (8 cases) confirms the mirror: a replayed attestation leaves the set at 1 entry and weight 2 of quorum 5.
findings.title: Attestation replay is safe by construction

findings.detail: The onNewAttestations documentation states that if the signer's list changes and a different subset has reached quorum, triggering that subset 'would require adding (or re-adding) an attestation that supports that subset.' A claim can therefore sit payable-but-untriggered, and claim ids carry no expiry, so a funded claim can wait indefinitely.
findings.title: A quorum reached after a signer-list change stays dormant until a new attestation arrives

findings.detail: finalizeClaimHelper divides the reward pool by the number of reward accounts. With fixXChainRewardRounding enabled the division rounds downward; without it (the live state) it uses the ambient Number::getround() mode. The code guards over-distribution with a tecINTERNAL return, so a claim that reached quorum can still fail at finalize time.
findings.title: Reward-split rounding fix is amendment-gated and disabled live

findings.detail: postfiat.org/pfusdc-trustless-bridge/ (HTTP 200, 68,866 bytes, fetched by the probe) describes a bridge with no committee, no multisig, and no signer: SP1 zkVM proofs of exact deposits/withdrawals verified on-chain against pinned checkpoints, demonstrated end-to-end on testnet (Arbitrum Sepolia withdrawal 0x664b2897…e702c1f9, exactly 1.000000 USDC released). The XChain code in postfiatd is upstream XRPL machinery; pfUSDC is a separate design in the postfiatl1v2 repository. The two must not be confused when assessing trust.
findings.title: The project's published bridge is pfUSDC, a proof-based design — not XChain

findings.detail: The XChainBridge.cpp header comment says 'See the document docs/bridge/spec.md for a full description of how bridges and their transactions work.' No docs/bridge/ directory exists in the pinned repository. Implementers have no in-repo specification; the upstream XRPL documentation is the only written reference.
findings.title: The in-repo bridge spec the code points to does not exist

findings.detail: A bridge keylet is indexHash(BRIDGE, door, currency), and no RPC method lists bridges; discovery requires knowing a door account and a currency in advance. The public feature RPC also exposes no amendment vote counts, so the activation approach for XChainBridge cannot be observed. The negative probes in this pack cover the only door pair the pinned code makes identifiable (genesis + masterpassphrase root over XRP).
findings.title: Bridges cannot be enumerated from the public surface

findings.detail: XChainCreateBridge preclaim returns tecNO_PERMISSION when the IOU issuer allows trust-line clawback (clawback would break the invariant that wrapped funds are always backed by locked funds), tecDUPLICATE when a bridge already exists for the door and currency, tecNO_ISSUER when the IOU issuer account does not exist, and tecINSUFFICIENT_RESERVE when the door account cannot afford the owner reserve.
findings.title: Clawback issuers and duplicate bridges are rejected at preclaim

findings.detail: Build 1.0.9, network 2025, validated ledger 8287770, complete ledgers 8200054-8287770, cadence 3.059 s/ledger, 21 peers, validation quorum 17, validator list sequence 30 with 25 validators, load factor 1, io latency 1 ms.
findings.title: Live network context at probe time
